decision: Thread resolverDeps (the full ResolverDeps interface containing keyedDigest) as an additive optional second parameter to createServer() and then to buildRouter(), where it is captured in a closure for use by any route that calls makeGrantResolver. startMain builds a single ResolverDeps object { keyedDigest } (from buildKeyedDigestFromEnv), passes it to createServer(), and places the SAME instance on MainHandle.resolverDeps — object identity by construction, not by coincidence. The e2e proof uses spec §8 pattern (b): resolveFor(handle.resolverDeps, ...) is called directly; the proof-of-equivalence comment in the test states that handle.resolverDeps is the exact allocation createServer received. No new HTTP route is added. No existing signature is broken (additive optional parameter). hash fields honestly degrade to drop when resolverDeps is absent (callers passing zero/one arg to createServer are unaffected).

rejected_alternatives.option: Add a minimal probe HTTP route (GET /api/resolve-probe) to drive a full HTTP socket through makeGrantResolver
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Gold-plating: spec FR-3 says additive only, no new routes beyond threading keyedDigest. A probe endpoint that exists only for testing is extra production surface. Spec §8 explicitly provides pattern (b) as a valid e2e proof — no socket required.

rejected_alternatives.option: Store resolverDeps in a module-level singleton in server.ts
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Hidden global state makes createServer non-re-entrant and non-testable with different deps. All other injected ports in this codebase use explicit parameter injection, not module-level globals.

rejected_alternatives.option: Read CHOROS_MASK_DIGEST_KEY inside buildRouter via process.env
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates FF-DC9 / NF-1 — process.env reads must stay exclusively in src/main.ts. Re-introduces the env boundary inside server.ts.

rejected_alternatives.option: Expose a makeResolver() factory on MainHandle and call it from the route
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Couples the request path back to the startup handle. Routes do not know about MainHandle — single-direction dependency enforced by the codebase conventions.

rejected_alternatives.option: Thread only { keyedDigest: KeyedDigest } rather than the full ResolverDeps
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Creates a second partial ResolverDeps shape and will require a signature change when the next optional port (classifications, effects, sod) is threaded. The full ResolverDeps interface is the established pattern; the optional type makes it backward-compatible today and extensible tomorrow.
